text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- ARGENTINA AND BRAZIL STRENGTHEN MERCOSUR

President Cardoso and his Argentine counterpart Carlos Menem met over the weekend and resolved a number of pending commercial disputes, while also announcing plans for further integration of the Mercosur customs union.
-- GOVT GUARANTEES CVRD AUCTION DATE

President Cardoso said the April 29 date for the privatization auction of state mining giant CVRD would not be changed and that government lawyers were appealing against Friday's court injunction which suspended the sell-off.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- TECHNICIANS WORK TO PREVENT NEW BLACKOUT
Power station technicians in the southeast of Brazil are working hard to prevent a third blackout tonight by finding the cause of Thursday's and Friday's blackouts.
-- CARDOSO ATTACKS CVRD OPPOSITION
President Cardoso criticized those who oppose the privatization of state mining giant CVRD, saying they did not understand the significance of the process underway which is a democratic one.
-- DEMONSTRATION FOR INDIAN ATTRACTS 1,500 IN BRASILIA
A demonstration in Brasilia in the same spot where a Brazilian Indian was torched to death by four youths a little more than a week ago attracted 1,500 people.
O GLOBO
-- FIRST DEFENDANT IN MASSACRE TRIAL GETS 449 YEARS
The first of 52 police officers to go on trial for allegedly gunning down arbitrarily 21 residents of Rio de Janeiro's Vigario Geral shantytown in August 1993 has been sentenced to 449 years in jail.
-- LANDLESS LEADERS PROPOSES DIALOG WITH GOVT
One of the leaders of Brazil's Landless Movement (MST) has taken on a more conciliatory tone and is pushing for greater dialog and understanding with the government.
-- Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom 5521 5074151))
